cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: cumulative beta distribution at x=2 with alpha=8, beta=10 on the interval [1,3]
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 0.6854706. Independently derived from the documented definition (the beta CDF rescaled to [A,B]): I_{(x-A)/(B-A)}(alpha,beta) = I_{0.5}(8,10), the regularized incomplete beta function, which scipy.special.betainc(8,10,0.5) gives as 0.6854705810546875 -> 0.6854706 at 7 dp

cases.description: The same parameters with cumulative FALSE, returning the probability density
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 1.4837646. Independently derived from the beta density rescaled to [A,B]: f((x-A)/(B-A); 8,10)/(B-A) = beta.pdf(0.5,8,10)/2 = 2.967529296875/2 = 1.4837646484374996 -> 1.4837646 at 7 dp

cases.description: The same distribution on the default interval, with A and B omitted
cases.expected_note: Excel documents "If you omit values for A and B, BETA.DIST uses the standard cumulative beta distribution, so that A = 0 and B = 1". Because x=2 on [1,3] rescales to exactly 0.5 on [0,1], this must return the identical 0.6854706 as the documented example -- a direct check of the documented default-bounds rule
Excel documents: "If alpha <= 0 or beta <= 0, BETA.DIST returns the #NUM! error value."

cases.description: An x value above the upper bound B
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If x < A, x > B, or A = B, BETA.DIST returns the #NUM! error value." Here x = 4 exceeds B = 3
Excel documents: "If any argument is nonnumeric, BETA.DIST returns the #VALUE! error value."
